candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — HIPAA/privacy of psychotherapy notes
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that HIPAA gives separately maintained psychotherapy notes special protection and generally requires patient authorization for use or disclosure, subject to limited regulatory exceptions.

options.A: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed whenever another person requests health information because they receive the same disclosure treatment as routine medical records.
options.B: Psychotherapy notes may be disclosed freely for treatment purposes because HIPAA never requires authorization when information is requested by another clinician.
options.C: Psychotherapy notes receive special protection, and with limited exceptions HIPAA generally requires the patient's authorization before use or disclosure.
options.D: Psychotherapy notes fall outside HIPAA because they are kept separately from the medical record, so federal privacy requirements do not apply to their release.

candidate.rationale: 45 CFR §164.508(a)(2) requires a covered entity to obtain authorization for uses or disclosures of psychotherapy notes except for limited enumerated circumstances. HHS also explains that separately maintained psychotherapy notes receive special protection and, with few exceptions, patient authorization is required before disclosure, including treatment disclosure to a clinician other than the note originator. C therefore states the rule accurately. A treats psychotherapy notes like ordinary records, B incorrectly creates a blanket treatment exception, and D incorrectly treats separate maintenance as exclusion from HIPAA.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Psychotherapy notes are specially protected; a covered entity generally must obtain patient authorization for use or disclosure, subject to limited enumerated exceptions; treatment disclosure to another clinician generally still requires authorization.
